content.rendered:
One of rock’s greatest riffs was based on another one of rock’s greatest riffs, and Bruce has played them both.

“Little Queenie” is the more common of the two (forever associated by fans with the infamous “bomb scare show” of 1975); Bruce’s version of “Get It On” is a lot more obscure.

The original, of course, is well-known and instantly recognizable. T. Rex released it as a single in 1971, and it went all the way to #10 in the U.S. and to the top spot in the U.K.

Supergroup The Power Station covered it in 1985, and their version (slightly retitled) charted as well, outperforming the original in the U.S.

When Bruce tackled it for the one and only time, it was with a supergroup of sorts, too. On the night of October 21, 1994, Bruce joined an all-star line-up at The Playpen in Sayreville, New Jersey.

Together with John Eddie, Greg Kihn, Marshall Crenshaw, and Elliott Murphy, Bruce tackled an impromptu “Bang a Gong (Get It On)” before seguing seamlessly into “(Get Your Kicks on) Route 66.” Listen to that one-time-only performance below.

Get It On
First performed: October 21, 1994 (Sayreville, NJ)
Last performed: October 21, 1994 (Sayreville, NJ)

© April 11, 2019

excerpt.rendered: One time only: Bruce Springsteen, John Eddie, Greg Kihn, Marshall Crenshaw, and Elliott Murphy team up on the T. Rex/Power Station classic.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Good Rockin’ Tonight
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Throughout the Darkness Tour, Bruce often announced his arrival with the song that announced the arrival of rock itself.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Sweet Little Sixteen
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Watch a great pro-shot video of Bruce covering Chuck Berry's classic 20 years after its release.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Summertime Blues
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With can't-catch-a-break lyrics belied by an infectious and instantly recognizable riff, "Summertime Blues" was tailor-made for a Springsteen set list. Watch some of Bruce's great performances of it inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: (Get Your Kicks On) Route 66
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Listen to two very different covers of "Route 66" recorded a half-century apart--both do justice to this 73-year-old R&B classic.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Let’s Go, Let’s Go, Let’s Go
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Days after Hank Ballard's passing, Bruces Springsteen and Hornsby (along with former Steel Mill bandmate Robbin Thompson) pay tribute by playing Ballard's last great hit.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Brown Eyed Girl
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce doesn't play "Brown Eyed Girl" often, but when he does, it's a singalong highlight, with no teleprompter required.
